root_cause.text: In the IPv6 FIB ECMP path, fib6_add_rt2node() incorrectly assumed every struct fib6_info contains an inlined trailing struct fib6_nh and dereferenced iter->fib6_nh without first checking the RTA_NH_ID case where iter->nh is used instead, causing an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “When IPv6 route is created with RTA_NH_ID, struct fib6_info does not have the trailing struct fib6_nh” and the fix changes `!iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family` to `(iter->nh || !iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family)`, explicitly guarding the dereference that triggered the KASAN slab-out-of-bounds in `fib6_add_rt2node()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix route flag clearing so IPv6 routes using `iter->nh` also have `RTF_ADDRCONF` and `RTF_PREFIX_RT` removed when appropriate.
intent_record.what: The condition inside fib6_add_rt2node() was changed from checking only `!iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family` to checking `(iter->nh || !iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family)` while keeping the surrounding `!(rt->fib6_flags & (RTF_ADDRCONF | RTF_PREFIX_RT))` test unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now clears `RTF_ADDRCONF` and `RTF_PREFIX_RT` on `iter` not only when the nexthop gateway family is unset, but also when `iter->nh` is present. This broadens the cases where those flags are removed, fixing handling for routes that use the `nh` field and preventing them from being treated as address-configured or prefix routes when they should not be.

grouping_result.intent: Fix route flag clearing so IPv6 routes using `iter->nh` also have `RTF_ADDRCONF` and `RTF_PREFIX_RT` removed when appropriate.

relevance_review.reason: The change targets the same RTA_NH_ID/`iter->nh` versus inlined `fib6_nh` distinction at the heart of the bug. Even though it fixes flag clearing rather than the exact dereference, it is directly caused by the incorrect assumption that every `fib6_info` uses the embedded nexthop.

candidates.rationale: This dereferences iter->fib6_nh unconditionally inside fib6_add_rt2node(). For routes using the RTA_NH_ID case, struct fib6_info does not have a valid inlined trailing fib6_nh there and uses iter->nh instead, so this access can read out of bounds.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally dereferences iter->fib6_nh in fib6_add_rt2node(). In the RTA_NH_ID case, struct fib6_info uses iter->nh instead of an inlined trailing fib6_nh, so accessing iter->fib6_nh can read beyond the valid object and trigger the out-of-bounds read described in the root cause.
